newsitem.title: USA: White House renews threat to veto abortion bill.
newsitem.headline: White House renews threat to veto abortion bill.

text.p: President Clinton's chief spokesman Friday said he was disappointed by the Senate's rejection of a White House-backed bill to curb late-term abortions, saying a Republican version was "clearly objectionable."
Clinton supported a bill drafted by Senate Democratic leader Tom Daschle that would have outlawed all late-term abortions except to save the life of the mother or avert grievous health consequences.

The Senate defeated it and a similiar measure offered Thursday by California Democrat Dianne Feinstein, paving the way for a vote next week on Pennsylvania Republican Rick Santorum's proposal to ban "partial birth" procedures at any point in pregnancy, except to save the life of the mother.
Clinton vetoed a nearly identical bill last year.

"I think (Clinton) was disappointed that Senator Daschle's alternative language didn't go forward because that was an attempt to accommodate the president's deeply held concerns," spokesman Mike McCurry said.
The defeated bills would have banned all late-term abortions, including partial birth, after a foetus is viable, or able to survive outside the uterus.
They would not have banned the partial birth procedure, also known as dilation and extraction, prior to viability. That procedure can be done in the fifth and sixth months.
"The Congress very clearly understands that the president objects to any ban that does not take into account the health needs of the mother," McCurry said.
Asked if Clinton's threat to veto the Santorum bill stood, the spokesman replied: "Yes, it does ... the Santorum bill is clearly objectionable."
